SOURCE = ThreeColoring
3-Coloring (graph 3-colorability).

  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.

Yes iff each vertex can be given one of 3 colours so that the two
endpoints of every edge get different colours. Not every colour has to

graph containing 4 mutually adjacent vertices (K4) is no.

Independent Set.

  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-kxavy6e0 && cat > reduce.py <<'EOF'
"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-Coloring to Independent Set.

Construction (standard "gadget" reduction):
  * For every vertex v of the source graph and every colour c in {0,1,2},
    create a target vertex (v, c), indexed as v*3 + c.
  * For every source vertex v, add edges between (v, c) and (v, c')
    for c != c', so an independent set can pick at most one colour per
    source vertex.
  * For every source edge {u, v} and every colour c, add an edge between
    (u, c) and (v, c), so adjacent source vertices cannot receive the
    same colour.

The source graph is 3-colourable iff the target graph has an independent
set of size n (one colour choice per source vertex).  Hence we set k = n.

Edge cases:
  * n = 0 -> target n = 0, k = 0, which is yes (k <= 0).
  * k = n <= 3 -> always yes, matching "any graph with <= 3 vertices is yes".
  * K4 -> no independent set of size 4, matching "K4 is no".
"""


def reduce(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]

    # Target graph has 3 nodes per source vertex.
    new_n = 3 * n
    new_edges = []

    def node(v, c):
        return 3 * v + c

    # At most one colour per source vertex.
    for v in range(n):
        for c1 in range(3):
            for c2 in range(c1 + 1, 3):
                new_edges.append([node(v, c1), node(v, c2)])

    # Adjacent source vertices must get different colours.
    for u, v in edges:
        for c in range(3):
            new_edges.append([node(u, c), node(v, c)])

    return {"n": new_n, "edges": new_edges, "k": n}
EOF

    tests_run += 1
    out = reduce(inst)
    IndependentSet.validate(out)
    expected = ThreeColoring.is_yes(inst)
    got = IndependentSet.is_yes(out)
    if expected == got:
        tests_passed += 1
    else:
        print("MISMATCH", inst, "->", out, "expected", expected, "got", got)

set of size n (one colour choice per source vertex).  Hence we set k = n.

  * n = 0 -> target n = 0, k = 0, which is yes (k <= 0).
  * k = n <= 3 -> always yes, matching "any graph with <= 3 vertices is yes".
  * K4 -> no independent set of size 4, matching "K4 is no".
"""


def reduce(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]

    # Target graph has 3 nodes per source vertex.
    new_n = 3 * n
    new_edges = []

    def node(v, c):
        return 3 * v + c

    # At most one colour per source vertex.
    for v in range(n):
        for c1 in range(3):
            for c2 in range(c1 + 1, 3):
                new_edges.append([node(v, c1), node(v, c2)])

    # Adjacent source vertices must get different colours.
    for u, v in edges:
        for c in range(3):
            new_edges.append([node(u, c), node(v, c)])

    return {"n": new_n, "edges": new_edges, "k": n}
